skill.name: hybrid-search-implementation
skill.description: Build hybrid search implementations that combine vector retrieval, keyword matching, fusion, and reranking for RAG and search applications.
skill.summary: Guides hybrid retrieval with RRF, pgvector, Elasticsearch, and RAG pipeline patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by search terminology, Markdown backticks, and tutorial headings. I found one high-risk semantic issue: the PostgreSQL example interpolates metadata keys into SQL. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: SQL identifier interpolation in the PostgreSQL metadata filter example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace dynamic metadata key interpolation with an allowlist of accepted JSON keys. Reject unknown keys before building SQL.

remediation.issue: Production hardening guidance is limited for copied templates.
remediation.suggestion: Add notes for input validation, query timeouts, result limits, and least-privilege database access before deployment.

semantic_findings.title: SQL Injection in Metadata Filter Example
semantic_findings.description: The PostgreSQL example interpolates metadata keys into SQL. If untrusted keys reach this template, an attacker could alter the SQL expression.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code parameterizes values but directly inserts the key into where_clause before conn.fetch. This is a clear SQL identifier injection risk in copied code.

content.value_statement: Single search methods miss exact terms or semantic matches. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical hybrid search patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to combine vector, keyword, and reranking search.
Provides RRF and weighted fusion implementation patterns.
Shows PostgreSQL pgvector and full-text search examples.
Shows Elasticsearch dense vector and BM25 examples.
Outlines a custom hybrid RAG pipeline with reranking.
Lists tuning and evaluation practices for retrieval quality.
limitations: Provides examples, not a complete production package.
Requires adaptation to the user storage clients and schemas.
Does not benchmark performance on the user corpus.
Some examples need security hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Improve RAG Retrieval
use_cases.description: Design retrieval that balances semantic matches with exact term recall before answer generation.

use_cases.title: Plan Search Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Compare pgvector, Elasticsearch, RRF, and reranking patterns for a new search service.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Ranking Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Review fusion options and choose a ranking strategy for product or support search.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether hybrid search fits my project. My corpus is [domain], queries are [types], and current failures are [examples].

prompt_templates.title: Design Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a hybrid search pipeline for [database or search engine]. Include indexing, retrieval steps, fusion, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Fusion
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me implement RRF for vector and keyword results. Use my data shapes: [describe result fields].

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my production hybrid RAG design for ranking quality, latency, observability, and security risks. Suggest concrete changes.

output_examples.input: I need exact product codes and semantic matches in support articles.
output_examples.output: A recommended hybrid design using BM25 for product codes, vectors for paraphrases, and RRF for final ranking.

output_examples.input: My vector search misses named entities.
output: Add keyword retrieval for names and rare terms.
Fuse keyword and vector candidates before reranking.
Measure recall on named-entity test queries.

output_examples.input: Choose between RRF and linear score fusion.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff summary that explains when RRF is easier and when calibrated scores justify linear fusion.

best_practices: Evaluate retrieval quality with representative queries before tuning weights.
Keep vector, keyword, and rerank scores visible in logs.
Validate filters and query inputs before building database queries.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on vector search alone for exact identifiers or rare names.
Do not copy templates into production without input validation and access controls.
Do not tune weights only on a small set of successful examples.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design hybrid retrieval that combines vector similarity, keyword search, fusion, and optional reranking.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete search service?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns that developers adapt to their storage layer and application.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: When should I use RRF?
faq.answer: Use RRF when result scores are hard to compare or when you need a strong default.

faq.question: Can it help with Elasticsearch?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes Elasticsearch dense vector and BM25 patterns.

faq.question: Is the sample code production ready?
faq.answer: No. Review security, validation, authentication, and performance before deployment.
